A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Psyche-R1, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 references Appendices A–C but ends after the references. V3 supplies appendices, leaving a localized gap in comparison of the earlier prompts and detailed settings.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on PCEB, CPsyExam and 200 sampled PsyDT items, together with training-stage ablations and a qualitative example.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports additional component ablations, difficulty-based analyses and a revised qualitative case study.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone, three-round prompt–rationale optimization, multi-LLM question selection, SFT/GRPO stages and reward functions are retained. Expanded curation descriptions and appendix prompts do not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Training retains the synthesized psychological questions and dialogues, PsycoLLM data and filtered CPsyExam training questions. Evaluation retains PCEB, CPsyExam and PsyDT counseling tasks. The new difficulty partitions and dataset-composition experiments operate within this coverage; Table 6 does not establish additional datasets being used.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 3 introduces random selection as a comparator for multi-LLM cross-selection. The evaluated LLM comparator sets in the corresponding benchmark and counseling tables remain unchanged after matching shortened names.

E3.justification: The main benchmark sizes, zero-/five-shot settings and stated training budgets are retained. V3 adds controlled training, supervision and data-composition variants, partitions PCEB by difficulty, and removes the counseling safety metric. Appendix B's decoding settings are newly disclosed, without establishing a change to the earlier evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The original SFT/SFT-plus-RL ablation expands substantially: v3 tests GRPO without SFT, answer-only versus rationale supervision, iterative refinement, random versus cross-selected questions, dataset mixtures and performance by difficulty (Tables 3–4; Figures 3–4). Appendix A also replaces the scientist's diagnostic-conflict example with a manager's counseling example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. V3 Table 3 adds relative percentage changes, which do not constitute uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial ablation and difficulty-based results, including Table 4's ED-only, PRD-only and combined averages of 51.11, 55.69 and 73.14. Main benchmark scores are largely retained, but GPT-4o's five-shot Case MMCQ entry changes from 52.50 to 51.50 in Table 2. The counseling safety entries are removed and the qualitative example changes. Revised Table 3 scores cannot be directly matched to v1's six-column ablation.

T1.justification: The SFT loss and piecewise accuracy reward retain their mathematical substance. The subset-notation change in the reward is equivalent because exact matches already occupy a separate branch. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first Chinese psychological LLM jointly integrating empathy, expertise and reasoning, using the same synthesis and hybrid-training contributions. The headline claim of a 7B model achieving performance comparable to DeepSeek-R1 is retained. Additional ablations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive cultural and language-transfer limitations, model-scale constraints, and explicit boundaries against diagnosis, treatment prescription and crisis intervention. It also adds interpretations concerning GRPO without prior SFT, complementary effects of reasoning data and empathetic dialogues, and larger gains on challenging questions. The case-study interpretation shifts toward counseling empathy and contextual expertise.

D1.justification: V3 supplies previously unavailable prompt templates, baseline identifiers, optimizer and scheduler details, PPO batching and KL settings, and decoding parameters in Appendices B–C. It adds a Psyche-R1 repository link and more specific curation/privacy disclosures, including semi-automatic student validation. The previously stated learning rates, batch sizes, epochs and GPU hardware are retained.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands cited context with STaR, newer mental-health reasoning and assessment systems, reasoning architectures, cultural and multimodal research, and efficient fine-tuning work. New Table 6 explicitly positions the dataset against prior psychological datasets through rationale, empathy and expertise coverage. The central novelty claim remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the exposition into numbered sections and subsections, separates ablations from discussion, and moves baseline and implementation descriptions into Appendix B. It rewrites and relocates the case study, revises methodological prose, and adds dedicated limitations, ethics and prompt sections.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain model-family groupings, parameter columns and colored highlighting. Table 3 changes from separate SMCQ/MMCQ columns to task-level scores and relative changes. New analysis charts, dataset and model-information tables, redesigned bilingual case displays and boxed appendix prompts substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility through Appendices B–C, adds useful dataset and selection controls, and states important clinical and cultural boundaries absent in v1. However, its revised Table 3 leaves the full-model Case score of 67.07 unexplained relative to the retained 63.31/56.26 standard accuracies in Table 1. This weakens the traceability of a central ablation and limits the otherwise positive overall improvement.
